deck.request: Is Harbour Credit Union growing safely, and how does it compare with its regional peers?
deck.brief: Is Harbour Credit Union growing safely against its regional peers?
deck.answer: Harbour is growing fast but not safely funded: it grows loans second-fastest of eight peers on the thinnest liquidity cover among them, 4.3 points above the regulatory minimum; its cost-to-income ratio keeps falling but its margin and capital sit mid-table, so term funding must come before further lending.

pages.title: Harbour is growing fast but not safely funded, so term funding must come first
pages.why: The opening states the answer and the three findings behind it, each with what it means for the plan

settles.what: growth, cash generation, liquidity cover and peer position against seven regional peers

pages.adds: Each point carries what its finding means for the plan, which the table does not show
pages.highlight: term funding must come before further lending
points: Loans grew {{A-loans/percent | 0%}} in seven years and {{A-loans-year/percent | 0.0%}} in FY26. Profit kept rising, but operating cash flow fell {{A-ocf/percent | 0% | abs}}, so earnings no longer pay for the growth.

Liquid assets now cover {{A-cover/result@FY26 | 0%}} of the liabilities due within a year, down every year from {{A-cover/result@FY22 | 0%}} in FY22 to {{A-floor/headroom | 0.0}} points above the regulatory minimum. Each loan funded with money due within a year lowers it again, so term funding must come before further lending.

Against its peers Harbour lends faster on thinner liquidity: second of eight on loan growth, last on cover, and fourth on margin and capital. Costs are not the risk: the cost-to-income ratio fell nine points.
The ranking rests on one year of regulatory returns, one union without a capital ratio: a guide to position, not a forecast.
